articleTitle: Advanced AI for Helianthus Disease Detection: A Hybrid CNN-KNN Model
abstract: The precise and prompt identification of diseases in sunflower crops is of utmost importance for the long-term viability of agriculture and the assurance of food supply. This study introduces an innovative methodology for the categorization of several diseases affecting helianthus plants, such as Rust, Wilt, Rot, and Stem Canker. The proposed strategy utilizes a hybrid deep learning model that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNN) and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) networks. By utilizing a varied dataset consisting of 25,000 high-resolution photos, our hybrid CNNKNN model attains a noteworthy overall accuracy rate of 95.78%. The incorporation of KNN layers in the model enables the consideration of temporal dynamics in the evolution of diseases, leading to a notable enhancement in the accuracy of disease classification. This improvement is particularly evident when differentiating between visually identical diseases, such as Rust and Stem Canker. The hybrid technique we propose has clear advantages when compared to solo CNN and KNN models, as evidenced by our comparative research. The research conducted in this study holds significant practical consequences as it presents a robust method for the automated diagnosis of diseases in sunflower crops. This tool has the potential to improve crop health and contribute to the promotion of sustainable agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Thermal Image Enhancement Techniques Using Histograms for Better Visualization of the Larynx and Vocal Folds
abstract: The noncontact localization of the vocal fold holds significant importance in intubation. Thermal cameras can aid in identifying potential issues and guiding the placement of the endotracheal tube during intubation by visually displaying temperature variations. This research paper primarily explores various image enhancement techniques, specifically those that employ histogram manipulation. The methods under investigation encompass Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization, Adaptive Histogram Equalization and Brightness Histogram Equalization. The central objective of this study is to assess the efficacy of these image enhancement techniques in improving the visibility and clarity of vocal fold images. Laryngoscopy is pivotal in medical procedures to examine and treat the larynx and throat. Laryngoscopy involves using a slender instrument known as a laryngoscope to visualize the internal structures of the larynx and throat. These image enhancement methods find valuable applications in optical and video laryngoscopy, aiding healthcare providers in achieving clearer and more precise visualization of the laryngeal and vocal cord regions.

articleTitle: Potato Leaf Disease Identification with Multi-Stage Approach: A Comparative Study
abstract: Potatoes are a vital source of food for people worldwide and are considered a staple food. However, potato diseases remain a significant concern for farmers as they can drastically reduce the yield and quality of harvests. Diseases such as Early Blight which can be seen on plant leaves are caused by Alternia Solani Fungi and microbes like Phytophthora Infestans De Bary causes disease like Late Blight and decreases total potato production. Disease identification and classification are essential for disease management, but it can be challenging for farmers to detect diseases early on due to the lack of expertise in the field. The method proposes a deep learning system which based on leaf conditions segregates diseases present in potato plants. The proposed method uses Digital Image Processing and a CNN architecture that helps to classify the diseases in potato plant leaves. Based on the models we proposed, we were able to achieve a bare minimum accuracy of 95%, which shows the promising potential of our model architectures. This method can help farmers detect diseases more accurately and earlier in the growth cycle, allowing for prompt management of the disease and reducing the risk of crop failure, making it a promising tool for farmers to improve the sustainability of potato farming.

articleTitle: Advanced Disease Management: An Encoder-Decoder Approach for Tomato Black Mold Detection
abstract: The global transmission of tomato black mold disease is a critical issue due to its substantial impact on agricultural productivity and the overall quality of crops. The prompt highlights the critical role of prompt and precise illness identification in facilitating effective disease control and promoting ecologically friendly farming practices. This paper presents a novel methodology for the timely identification of black mold infestation in tomatoes. The proposed strategy utilizes a dense dilated convolution technique included inside an encoder-decoder architecture. The process of feature extraction utilizes the widely recognized VGG-16 model. Our model, on the other hand, has been trained and assessed using a rigorously curated dataset consisting of 25,000 tomato photos, which were collected by our team. The model has exceptional performance in accurately segmenting and precisely localizing contaminated areas, as indicated by the significantly high values of the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and Intersection over Union (IoU). Furthermore, the model's capacity to estimate ground truth boundaries is emphasized by the minimal Hausdorff Distance. Our research not only makes a significant contribution to the assurance of food safety but also advances the field of precision agriculture by providing farmers with a dependable method for disease identification. Our suggested method utilizes advanced computer vision techniques and deep learning (DL) models to enable the early and accurate detection of tomato black mold disease. This advancement has the potential to support sustainable crop management practices and provide significant benefits to the agricultural community.

articleTitle: Analysing Various Compensation Schemes for Inductive Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: Electric vehicles are becoming more and more important as demand for automobiles rises and internal combustion engines face issues. Wireless charging is a suitable and reliable approach among the several Electric Vehicle (EV) charging strategies. The most popular Wireless Power transmission (WPT) techniques are inductive and capacitive power transmission. A poorly connected primary and secondary coil makes it more difficult to maintain a high efficiency in an inductively coupled energy transfer system. A compensating circuit is linked to both the coils in order to enhance performance. In this study, simulation in MATLAB Simulink is used to compare several compensation topologies for charging a battery.

articleTitle: Hybrid Clutter Suppression Technique for FOPEN Target Imaging Radar
abstract: This paper presents a detailed exploration of Foliage Penetration Radar (FOPEN) technology, focusing on its advancements, challenges, and experimental implementation. Outlining the fundamental principles of radar, underscores the critical role of FOPEN radar in detecting objects concealed beneath dense vegetation. It delves into the challenges faced by FOPEN systems, particularly in discriminating between man-made targets and natural features within vegetation, emphasizes ongoing research efforts to optimize radar frequencies, improve signal processing algorithms. Linear Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (LFMCW) FOPEN radar system is indigeneously designed, providing insights into its architecture and capabilities. Also, proposed methodology implementing Hybrid Clutter Suppression including noise removal, Doppler processing, and target detection, showcasing promising results in detecting concealed targets behind light foliage. The adaptability of the LFMCW-based FOPEN radar system, as demonstrated in the experimental results, positions it as a valuable tool for applications ranging from military surveillance to civilian geospatial imaging in challenging environments. A research for such systems can be pursued with a focus on minimizing false alarms, understanding the environmental impact, and exploring humanitarian and environmental monitoring applications of FOPEN radar.

articleTitle: Photonic Sensor for the Detection of Hemoglobin in Blood for Development of Point of Care Diagnostics
abstract: Recent pandemic has shown the lack of medical infrastructure worldwide. Development of cost-effective point of care devices will increase the accessibility of medical infrastructure. Currently in use, point of care bio technological devices has ability to detect only single parameter. Photonic sensing technology has come as a viable solution as it has an ability to detect changed components in the blood. In this research, we designed an optical biosensor which is able to detect levels of oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin concentration. The biosensor is based on photonic crystal, which allows improved light matter interactions. When the air in the photonic crystal is replaced by the hemoglobin and is excited with light, a spectrum of captured at the other end. Clear shift is observed in the power in the spectrum for different levels of the hemoglobin and is line with respect to concentration levels. The variation in the power absorption with respect to refractive index (RI) and frequency is observed. The designed sensor is highly sensitive with optimized Q factor. The design can be further developed in to a Lab-On-A-Chip environment to detect multiple components simultaneously.

articleTitle: Visual Sentinel: Data Analytics for Missing Subject Identification
abstract: The goal of the “Visual Sentinel: Video Analytics for Missing Subject Identification” project is to automate the process of identifying missing subjects from CCTV video by utilizing cutting-edge machine learning and computer vision techniques. One of the project's goals is to create a real-time surveillance system that integrates face recognition technology for increased precision and accuracy. The technology has the ability to save lives and bring families back together by speeding up the search and recovery procedure. To effectively locate missing subjects, the system uses de-blurring methods and machine learning algorithms. The technology effectively matches people in real-time against a specified data collection, giving authorities access to timely information, according to key results. To sum up, Visual Sentinel provides a strong and practical solution that enables security and law enforcement professionals.

articleTitle: Nanomaterial Based Biosensor for Diabetic Applications
abstract: This paper introduces a U-shaped fiber sensor incorporating a silver nanoparticles coating on its surface, demonstrating remarkable sensitivity to small molecules, particularly glucose. The nanoparticles synthesis involved 339.74 mg of AgNO3 (silver nitrate) and 516.12 mg of sodium citrate in a 1-liter solution. Experimental observations revealed that as the concentration of glucose increased, the refractive index of the fiber decreased, leading to power loss. The sensor's fabrication comprised three key stages. Initially, silver nanoparticles were synthesized. Subsequently, the fiber was characterized, and the nanoparticles were applied to its surface. In the final stage, glucose oxidase was incorporated for glucose detection. The experiments determined a maximum power loss of 0.5 μW at a glucose concentration of 0.6 molar.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fabric Integrity: Seg-YOLO-Based Defect Detection in Handloom Fibers
abstract: Handloom fabrics hold significant cultural and economic importance worldwide. Ensuring the quality and integrity of these fabrics is essential, as defects can affect their market value and consumer satisfaction. The paper proposes an innovative approach for detection and segmentation of defects in handloom fabrics using a novel model known as “Seg-YOLO.” It combines the efficiency of YOLO (You Only Look Once) framework with the precision of pixel-level segmentation. The network is trained to simultaneously detect defects and provide fine-grained segmentation of defect regions within the fabric. By fusing it offers a comprehensive solution for identifying various defect types, including irregular weaves, stains, and tears, with high accuracy and efficiency. In experimental evaluations, our model excels in real-time processing, making it suitable for use in manufacturing environments and quality control processes. This research will represent a significant step forward in the domain of handloom fabric inspection, offering a robust and automated solution for the detection and segmentation of defects.

articleTitle: Transforming the Prediction of Heart Disease: An Empirical Analysis of Machine Learning Classifiers
abstract: The most prevalent diseases impacting the lives of individuals are those connected to the human body's most critical organ, the heart. It is crucial to emphasize that heart disease problems are not a new phenomenon and should not be sought after or welcomed as a trend, even if heart-related issues have received more attention and debate in recent years as a consequence of increased understanding and research. By leveraging their data processing and analytical skills, computers, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the internet have revolutionized the identification and prediction of cardiac disease. The suggested model is evaluated and compared to current models that have been shown to be more accurate and effective, such as K-nearest Neighbor, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Random Forest and many other machines learning and deep learning Logistic Regression, Random Forest, K- nearest Neighbor and Decision Tree. After comparing and testing many models using various criteria, Random Forest revealed that the suggested model had the greatest accuracy 82.72%.

articleTitle: Silage Density Prediction Using Neural Network
abstract: Silage., a form of livestock feed., is produced using fresh green foliage crops. The preservation of silage involves fermentation until it reaches an acidified state., making it suitable for feeding farm animals. Good quality forage has benefits in decreasing feed costs and lowering harvest losses. Its compaction is essential to produce high-quality grass silage. Understanding the quality of forage in grasslands is essential for aligning with the requirements of animal nutrition. In this paper the silage compaction sensing is proposed using cutting-edge m-sequence UWB (ultra-wideband) radar technology which illustrates behavior of test material using impulse response function. Experiment has been performed to collect UWB radar reflections with different silage materials such as grass and corn. For the analysis, data driven framework is created using python and MATLAB. Neural network model built on this data has shown confidence when it is tested for unknown silage density. The calculated density is closely correlated with the ground reference and based on results from a silage compaction sensing algorithm, proposed method found to be favorable for the prediction of the silage density.

articleTitle: Automative Feedback System for Descriptive Answers in LMS using Machine Learning Algortihm
abstract: This study describes a learning management system (LMS) designed to enhance theoretical assessments and provide students with detailed, descriptive feedback. The LMS is comprised of two interconnected systems serving distinct functions. The first system concentrates on assigning grades to student work, while the second provides detailed, descriptive feedback. The undertaking involves the integration of two machine-learning models into the LMS website. By automating the evaluation of explanatory the motive is to give appropriate feedback to the students thought which they can reflect upon their errors and learn from them. By automating the evaluation of explanatory responses and providing immediate feedback, the project seeks to improve the efficacy of educational assessment procedures.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Thin Film Holographic Metasurface-Based Leaky wave Antenna
abstract: A holographic metasurface-based leaky wave antenna (HMLA) is presented in this paper. The proposed metasurface, which is based on the holographic principle, is capable of transforming an omnidirectional monopole into a directional leaky wave antenna. A polyimide (PI) thin film (Dk = 3.05, Df = 0.008) having a thickness of 50μm has been employed for the holographic metasurface. Following the top PI metasurface layer is a 40 μm thick adhesive layer (Dk = 6, Df = 0.004), followed by the Rogers RT 5880 substrate layer (Dk = 2.20, Df = 0.0009) with 1.6 mm thickness grounded at the bottom. The antenna is designed for 15 GHz, directional radiation, and beam steering at ɵ = 10° by implementing the intended metasurface.

articleTitle: Incorporating Innovative Teaching-Learning for Analog Circuit Design Course
abstract: The course, Analog Circuit Design is compulsory professional basic core course for engineering majors such as Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering, which aims to cultivate students' innovation ability and engineering practice ability, stimulate their interest and motivation in learning, and help them appreciate the spirit of teamwork. When following the conventional teaching methodology, most of the students find difficulty in understanding the concepts of circuit design specially in applying the concepts into real problem solving. It happens due to the coverage of a wide topic in insufficient time frame, where teacher mainly focuses on the lecture based theoretical teaching. But traditional teaching method can't enable maximum students to effectively master the knowledge of analog circuits. To solve this issue, along with the lecture parts, teacher-student interactive activities have been followed. In view of the issues existing in the conventional teaching mode, this paper addresses a few teaching-learning methodologies adopted like word cloud preparation, Think-pair-share activity, question-answer writing skill development towards a question-answer-bank, technology based learning (mini-project) etc. At the end of the course, a student feedback analysis has been done which shows that more than 60% students responded positively about the innovative teaching learning methodologies incorporated for this course.

articleTitle: Opto-Electronic Oscillator Design for Photonic Radar System
abstract: Research in photonic generation of microwave signals, particularly through opto-electronic oscillator (OEO)-based techniques, has thrived over the last three decades. These methods employ varied OEO designs, incorporating optical components like optical fiber, polarization modulators, chirped fiber Bragg gratings and ring resonators. Various OEO schemes have been developed to enhance spectral purity, aiming for ultra-low phase noise in the generation of single-frequency RF signals. In this paper two different schemes of OEOs are simulated in OptiSystem and we achieved 60 dBm gain for single loop OEO and 83 dBm gain for dual loop OEO at 10 GHz. Conducting signal-to-noise ratio analysis, histogram analysis, and assessing phase noise stability serves as a comprehensive approach to substantiate and validate the efficacy of these OEOs and finally a 10 GHz OEO is developed and experimentally demonstrated in our laboratory for photonic radar system.

articleTitle: Detection of Thoracic Diseases Using Chest X-Ray: A Comparative Study of Binary Class and Multiclass Classification Using Deep Learning
abstract: Identifying thoracic ailments stands pivotal in medical imaging, offering insights for disease recognition and treatment. Chest X-ray (CXR) imaging emerges as a prevalent non-invasive and cost-effective technique for thoracic disease detection [1–4]. This research delves into a comparative exploration between binary class and multiclass classification methodologies in identifying thoracic diseases through CXR images. Our approach involves training and assessing deep learning models leveraging a publicly accessible CXR image dataset, juxtaposing the performance of binary and multiclass models using diverse performance metrics. We formulated 17 distinct binary class models and orchestrated their ensemble, alongside crafting a solitary multiclass classification model [25–26]. The assessment of these models encompassed various performance metrics, including F1 score, accuracy, precision, and recall. The outcomes advocate for binary classification's pragmatic suitability, attributed to its heightened accuracy and simplified implementation. This inquiry strives to refine the precision and efficacy of CXR image analysis in clinical practice.

articleTitle: Web-based Emergency Alert System for Driver's Drowsiness and Medical Exigency
abstract: Fatigue in car or other commercial vehicle drivers is a significant contributor to road accidents globally. Due to lack of sleep and other illnesses, drivers may experience drowsiness or other medical issues, which can cause fatal accidents. This paper presents a comprehensive driver assistance system that addresses driver fatigue, detecting drowsiness and medical emergencies, alarm and assistance, and emergency alerts. The methodology includes using the Haar cascade classifier for drowsiness detection, driver's heart rate monitoring through a smartwatch, and a CNN-based facial expressions detection that helps predict medical emergency conditions. The proposed system generates regular text and audio alarm alerts for the driver. The Google Maps platform gives nearby hotels and hospital assistance to drivers. Furthermore, an autonomous EAS is implemented to notify emergency services and the driver's emergency contacts, potentially saving lives in critical situations. The system is implemented as a streamlit-based web application that acts as a visual interface for the driver. The proposed comprehensive driver assistance system can contribute to reducing road accidents caused by driver fatigue, help save lives and promoting road safety in society.

articleTitle: A Bow-Tie shaped Slot Antenna with Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) and Periodic Patches for Gain and Bandwidth Improvement
abstract: A bow-tie slot antenna with (SIW) Substrate Integrated Waveguide and periodic parasitic patches to improve gain and bandwidth is presented. The presented antenna structure is 0.74 λ<inf>0</inf> x 1.09 λ<inf>0</inf> x 0.028 λ<inf>0</inf> in size. The conventional slot antenna has bidirectional radiation pattern, this bidirectional radiation pattern becomes unidirectional by incorporating SIW structure. By placing periodic patches at the bottom of the antenna it refines gain and bandwidth. The presented antenna exhibits bandwidth of 0.85 GHz (9.128 GHz – 9.178 GHz), moderate gain of 7.79 dBi is obtained. The resonance frequency of antenna is 9.55 GHz having a return loss of -27.22 dB. The simulation of the Antenna is done using HFSS 19.1 software which has flat gain response making it suitable for X band application.

articleTitle: Application of Levenberg-Marquardt Algorithm in Neural Network Based Actual Engine Torque Estimation and Monitoring
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for predicting gasoline engine torque using a neural network model based on the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (LMA). The model generates an engine torque map by considering engine speed and throttle angle as input variables. To assess its reliability, the technique is validated using a dataset comprising 23,450 real-world gasoline engine data points for training, validation, and testing. The results demonstrate the model's ability to accurately predict and map engine torque at short time intervals. This method significantly enhances the efficiency of monitoring systems in automotive vehicles' functional safety domain by providing precise torque map values through appropriate interpolations.

articleTitle: Digital Implementation of Depthwise Separable Convolution Network for AI Applications
abstract: Convolutional neural networks(CNN) have gained widespread popularity in the fields of computer vision and pattern recognition due to their exceptional accuracy. However, the computational demands of operating large convolutions often necessitate powerful computing platforms like a Graphical Processing Unit (GPU), making it challenging to utilize CNNs on portable devices. To address this issue, advanced CNN models such as MobileNetV2 and Xception employ Depthwise Separable Convolution(DSC) instead of Standard Traditional Convolution(STC) for embedded systems. This approach significantly reduces computations and parameters while only marginally sacrificing accuracy. This innovative model structure is particularly well-suited for implementation on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays(FPGAs). In our research paper, we propose DSc accelerator within CNNs. The design allows flexibility in adapting to FPGAs of various sizes, achieving an excellent balance between hardware resource utilization and processing speed efficiency. We have successfully implemented this using the Verilog Hardware Description Language(HDL), and We have achieved the corresponding outcomes for an image size of 256 × 256 × 3.

articleTitle: Mayfly Algorithm Optimized FOPID Regulator for Frequency Improvement in Wind Power Systems
abstract: The purpose of this article is to discuss frequency improvement in wind power systems (WPS). The result of the Mayfly algorithm (MA) to frequency enhancement is studied in the WPS with the support of secondary controllers PID and FOPID controllers (proportional-integral-derivative and fractional-order PID). The autonomous WPS includes a battery energy storage system (BESS) to aid the secondary controller. The responsiveness of the suggested approach to frequency variation was investigated in the MATLAB, Simulink working environment with a 1% load disturbance. The control response of the MA-FOPID and PID controllers is compared with the results of standard optimization techniques to show the preeminence of the proposed technique. The evaluation of the results indicates that the MA technique performs better than other optimization techniques for frequency improvement.

articleTitle: Solanaceae Family Plants Disease Classification Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: The Solanaceae family's tomato and potato crops are particularly vulnerable to early blight and late blight. These two diseases greatly reduce the crop yield. Here, authors consider potato crop samples for rapid and accurate diagnosis of potato leaf diseases. Visual inspection is the most challenging task for farmers for deworming. In this paper, for the diagnosis of potato plant leaf diseases, two automatic detection methodologies are proposed. In the first approach, gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) and 2-D discrete wavelet transform applied to extract features from leaf images and support vector machine, logistic regression, and K-nearest neighbors machine learning techniques are applied for classification. In second approach, convolutional neural networks are applied to identify diseases. The findings show that the convolutional neural networks-based model beats its competitor techniques in various evaluation parameters. The convolutional neural networks based model achieves the best accuracy 97%, followed by SVM 93 %, logistic regression 91 % and KNN 89%. The proposed method will undoubtedly assist farmers in identifying crop disease and take timely decisions for protection.

articleTitle: Penetration Testing of Smart Meters against Cyber Attacks
abstract: Smart Meters and Smart Grids are the present and future of power, water, and gas distribution systems around the world. The Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, which is an automated remote command and control system, form the backbone of these smart grids. This makes smart meters and SCADA systems highly lucrative target for cyber-attacks for any organisation/country. For the communication in a smart grid to be secure, it must provide confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the data from end-to-end. Various defence mechanisms for a few types of cyber-attacks on a SCADA system are proposed. For the defenders, it becomes extremely important to plug the vulnerabilities and make the Smart Grids more robust to counter such attacks. Study of vulnerabilities of SCADA systems has been the focus. Work has been carried out with the help of experiments and thereby brought out a few vulnerabilities which are critical to the security of SCADA systems. Using an experimental smart grid various cyber-attacks have been demonstrated successfully which includes Man-in-the-Middle and Denial-of-Service attacks. Possible counter-measures are proposed for protection against such types of attacks.

articleTitle: Enhanced 3D Scene Reconstruction Using Synchronized Multiple Kinect Depth Cameras
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to enhance the accuracy of 3D scene reconstruction using multiple depth cameras. The challenge of a limited field of view, which hinders the correct reconstruction of occluded parts, especially in dynamic scenes, is addressed. To overcome this limitation, the paper proposes the simultaneous use of multiple depth cameras. To address IR interference that arises between multiple depth cameras, the method suggests the use of software-based time-division multiplexing for each depth camera. The proposed method employs a plane segmentation-based extrinsic calibration algorithm to coarsely align the view of each depth camera. This coarse alignment facilitates the integration process, enabling existing registration algorithms like Go-ICP to more accurately fuse views from each depth camera. We validate our proposed extrinsic calibration method for 3D reconstruction using multiple depth cameras, particularly focusing on its impact on the accuracy and speed of registration. The experimentation involves fusing views from two Kinect cameras with and without extrinsic calibration using the Go-ICP algorithm. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed extrinsic calibration in enhancing 3D reconstruction performance.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Software Tool for Audio Signal-based Hinglish to English Language Translation
abstract: Most of the current Indian generation speaks/writes using Hinglish on various social media platforms. It is difficult to understand and interpret Hinglish using existing computational linguistic tools mainly based on English. Hence, there is a need to provide automated Hinglish to English Language Translation tools to integrate with existing NLP-based applications like hate speech detection. Currently, such complex language translations are manually intensive and require domain experts. Also, there is a scarcity of standard datasets in this domain for carrying out helpful research. In this research, we propose an intelligent AI-based translator for translating audio data signals from Hinglish to English, which can be integrated into various NLP-based applications in the Indian Context. We also created a large-scale customized annotated Hinglish to English dataset containing 27135 entries of size 4.121MB. After extensive experimentation, we received the highest BLEU (Bi-Lingual Evaluation Understudy) score of 92.20 on our customized Hinglish to English dataset, while on the original PHINC dataset, we found a BLEU score of 70 approx. We also developed a Python TKinter-based user-friendly GUI application that takes audio signal/voice as input and provides English-translated text as output.

articleTitle: Role of Engineering Projects in Prospective of Teaching-Learning Process
abstract: Project based learning is a pedagogy that enhances the teaching learning process by focusing on current edge technologies through group learning. The students will be made aware to identify the various problems and device feasible solutions for the same. The main objective is to make student learn to identify the problem and approach to the solution. Subsequently students will acquire technical skills to implement the solution. Engineering projects emerge as dynamic bridges between classroom instruction and real- world application. Moreover, they foster the cultivation of critical skills such as design thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, communication, and project management, all of which are paramount for success in the engineering profession. Beyond skill development, engineering projects have a profound impact on students' motivation and engagement, offering them a sense of ownership and purpose in their learning journey. This paper underscores the adaptability of engineering projects across different disciplines and educational levels, showcasing their versatility as transformative tools for learning. It also emphasizes the essential role of mentors and instructors in guiding students through these projects, enhancing the educational experience and nurturing a culture of mentorship within the engineering community.

articleTitle: Fingerprint Quality Metric Fusion Framework
abstract: The task to categorize a fingerprint image based on its quality from the point of view of higher matching scores is non-trivial. Here we propose a fusion framework by using standard score normalization to fuse the quality scores from two or more metrics. The framework for creation of new quality metric for fingerprint is evaluated using error reject curves for FVC2002 DB1A database. Also, the framework of fingerprint quality metric is evaluated for the purpose of reconstructing fingerprints from the minutia features.

articleTitle: Multi Criteria Decision Making in Fantasy Sports
abstract: Football is a very famous sport worldwide and continues gaining traction to this day. As the interest in the game rises, so do the methods of interacting with the game. One such avenue is the FPL (Football Premier League). Recent years have seen a huge spike in interest for virtual, fantasy playing applications like the FPL. A person participating is usually heavily biased towards certain players or teams. This inherent bias causes them to make certain irrational decisions which may not provide the best results. There exists a huge gap in the market for an algorithm-based approach to team selection and the aim of this research is to make an optimal application capable of filling that void. The premise of this research is to create a team recommender system that optimizes one's team selection strategy for the FPL. This research works by introducing objectivity and eliminating biases in the team selection process. It incorporates the usage of TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) and criteria-based metrics along with an XG-Boost regression predictor, with the aim of filling the gaps in the current systems and to maximize the returns while minimizing the cost associated with it. The approach implemented involved the usage of XGBoost, yielding a standard deviation of 0.041188.

articleTitle: A Linear Closed Loop Feedback System for Beam Wander Correction in Medium-Range Optical Link
abstract: Free Space Optical Communication (FSOC) is gaining popularity as a viable solution in various applications due to the advantages it offers in terms of bandwidth, EMI immunity, security, cost and deployment time. Being a Line-of-Sight (LoS) technology, it is of utmost importance that the alignment between the transmitter and the receiver is maintained. After the optical link is attained, the laser beam displacement due to the beam wander has to be mitigated. A laser beam stabilisation system, employing a Fast Steering Mirror (FSM), a position sensor and a controller to form a linear closed loop feedback system to correct the positional error in real time is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Irrigation Management in Smart Agriculture
abstract: This paper introduces a pioneering approach to modernize agricultural practices through the integration of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) into irrigation management. The primary objectives include achieving accurate data analysis for precise irrigation control, implementing real-time data collection and monitoring, and developing a decision support system that leverages ANN insights to enhance crop health and resource efficiency. The utilization of ANN represents a cutting-edge advancement in smart agriculture, harnessing the capabilities of deep learning and attention mechanisms to optimize irrigation strategies. To build the ANN model, training data is collected and utilized to the objective is to train three models: The Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), along with the proposed Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. This study assesses the efficacy of the suggested model and conducts a comparative analysis with the support provided by CNN and LSTM algorithms. The ANN model emerged as the standout performer across all metrics. With an accuracy of 97.24%, it outperformed both the LSTM (95.68<sup>%</sup>) and CNN (93.39<sup>%</sup>), showcasing its superior capability in accurately classifying temperature and moisture data, critical for precise irrigation management. Moreover, the ANN model demonstrated exceptional specificity and sensitivity values at 96.08% and 95.98%, respectively, surpassing both CNN and LSTM models.

articleTitle: Enhanced Vulnerability Discovery in Embedded Firmware Binaries Through Function-Level Fuzzing
abstract: With the proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, the security of their firmware has emerged as a critical concern. This paper proposes the use of instrumentation techniques for function-level fuzzing. By employing instrumentation techniques, such as dynamic binary instrumentation (DBI), it demonstrates the benefits of fuzzing of an individual function within ARM binary of ELF format. The paper presents advantages of proposed technique over traditional whole-binary fuzzing approaches. The advantages include reduction in the fuzzing scope thereby resulting in improved time efficiency and reduced resource requirements. The proposed technique is implemented on an ARM based embedded hardware i.e Raspberry Pi thus demonstrating its ability to be implemented on IoT devices.

articleTitle: Hybridization Unleashed: Advancing Movie Recommendations Through Collaborative, Content Based and Hybrid Filtering
abstract: A vast amount of data is available for customers to explore, making it challenging to sift through and find relevant solutions according to their preferences. Recommendation systems offer a way to filter out important information from irrelevant content and provide personalized suggestions to customers. Recently, there's been a growing interest in creating recommendation systems that suggest movies and books based on user preferences due to the surge in digital content. However, existing systems usually focus solely on movies or books, neglecting cross-domain recommendations. To overcome these constraints, the present study introduces a hybrid movie recommendation system. By amalgamating collaborative and content-based filtering, this system strives to provide users with more accurate and varied suggestions. Through experimentation using a dataset comprising movies and books, the findings reveal that the proposed system surpasses traditional collaborative and content-based filtering approaches in both accuracy and diversity. Additionally, the system effectively tackles the cold-start issue associated with a lack of data for new users or items. With its potential to extend beyond movies, this hybrid recommendation system holds the promise of providing personalized and diverse recommendations across various domains.

articleTitle: Lightweight Authentication Protocols for IoT Networks
abstract: As the internet is developing day by day, the Internet of Things(IoT) is emerging as a very promising technology in many industries. It becomes very important to make sure the confidentiality, integrity and authenticity of data being transmitted in the IoT network. To enhance the security and privacy in the IoT domain, interaction among users over the internet while exchanging sensitive data, may require an authenticated transmission network. After conducting a literature review, found that the sensitive data exchanged between communication channels are in-secure and the cost of transmission and computation is very high. Identity based cryptography eliminated the problem of public certificate management and elliptic curve cryptography minimize the communication and computation cost rather than using any symmetric key cryptography. And proposed a lightweight authentication protocol in IoT network using identity based cryptography and elliptic curve cryptography and established a secure session key between users in public channel.

articleTitle: Balance Relation-Aware Attention Embedding Model for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Predicting missing links has great significance in knowledge graph completion because it helps improve the accuracy and completeness of the information in the graph. The recent models employ an attention mechanism to capture the graph network. Previous attention-based models treat similar relation semantics for associated pairs of entities, but relations might have similar names but represent different semantics. Thus, models fail to capture the semantic dissimilarity of relations involved within the triplet entity pair. This paper proposes a new graph attention model capable of effectively learning embeddings by combining relationship features with triplet entity embeddings to balance relationship contributions while capturing meaningful graph structure. The model incorporates relational compositional embeddings to determine distinct attention for neighboring nodes during computation and update the entity embedding. This novel approach outperforms the previously established models on the benchmark dataset.

articleTitle: Throttle Less Electric Bicycle Controller Using Fuzzy Logic
abstract: Traveling has become an essential aspect of modern life, with electric bicycles (E-bicycles) witnessing widespread adoption due to their eco-friendliness and energy-efficient operation. This research paper introduces an innovative method to improve the control system of E-bicycles by incorporating a controller that operates without a throttle. By combining the power of fuzzy logic and deep learning, we aim to eliminate the need for throttle input and conventional switching modes, ultimately enhancing rider experience and optimizing battery consumption. Our proposed controller integrates load, velocity, and gradient sensors to gather real-time data, and employs a fuzzy logic-based decision-making mechanism to regulate the motor's power output. This approach demonstrates the potential to revolutionize E-bicycle control, offering smoother rides and reduced energy consumption.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control with Power Frequency Compensation for Pumped Storage Hydropower Stations
abstract: This paper explores the impact of variable structure controllers (VSC) and pumped storage hydro power stations on the frequency stability of a two-area power system. A comprehensive simulation model is developed to evaluate the system's response to load disturbances. The findings reveal that the implementation of VSC controllers yields significant improvements in frequency stability compared to conventional Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) controllers. The frequency deviation is reduced by an impressive 43%, demonstrating the remarkable effectiveness of VSC controllers in regulating and maintaining system frequency. Furthermore, the integration of pumped storage hydro power stations into the system enhances its frequency response characteristics, resulting in minimized frequency deviations during generating operations. This synergistic combination of VSC controllers and pumped storage units offers a highly promising and robust approach to achieve reliable frequency regulation and mitigate the adverse effects of load disturbances in power systems. These results underscore the vital role of advanced control strategies and renewable energy storage solutions in ensuring a stable, resilient, and sustainable electricity supply.

articleTitle: The Conglomerate Compression Approach for Visual Pattern Recognition Networks in Edge AI Applications
abstract: Deep Neural Networks have shown remarkable performance in various applications of Visual Pattern Recognition (VPR). This field continues to grow due to emergence of new architectures, availability of huge data, and powerful computing resources. However, because of their high computational complexity that subsequently demands higher memory requirements, and power consumption, the deployment of such DNN-based Visual Pattern Recognition Networks (VPRN) models in edgeAI applications is hindered. Such overheads necessitate the compression of VPRN models while retaining their performance. This paper explores multiple compression techniques which combines Knowledge Distillation (KD), pruning and quantization that are applied to DNNs to achieve higher compression ratio.

articleTitle: Classification of Underwater Sea Species Using Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: The importance of recognizing fish species has increased as a result of new marine science research. Classifying fish species manually requires a person who has knowledge about all the species and this is a time consuming process. The classification of fish species could be automated using technology, advancing marine science. Deep learning techniques have led to an increase in the number of image classification tasks. In this paper we have compared performance of proposed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model with existing CNN architectures for classification of LifeClef 2015 Fish (LCF-15) dataset. This dataset consist of 15 different classes of sea species and total number of images are 22444. It is observed that the proposed model achieves accuracy of 98.76%. The proposed model is light weight, having less number of parameters and flops compared to other existing models. The precision, recall and f1-score achieved for the proposed model are 98.78%,98.76% and 98.71 % respectively.

articleTitle: CogniDrip: Real-time Saline Infusion Management with Measurement and Alert System
abstract: It is essential for healthcare settings to manage saline infusion in an effective and efficient manner to ensure patient safety and the best possible treatment outcomes. CogniDrip is an innovative solution that addresses the challenges associated with traditional methods of saline bottle monitoring, which can lead to inefficiency and disruption of patient care. The system combines advanced sensing technology and intelligent alert mechanisms to provide continuous automated monitoring of the remaining saline volume in infusion bottles. This system accurately measures the remaining volume of saline and predicts when the bottle will run out, significantly reducing the risk of abrupt interruption of the infusion process. Additionally, the system quickly alerts nursing staff via customizable notifications, allowing for timely replacement and avoiding treatment interruptions. The implementation of CogniDrip in healthcare facilities can not only improve patient safety, but also optimize resource allocation by reducing unnecessary staff interventions. Its adaptability, user-friendly interface, and practicality make it an ideal solution for widespread implementation. CogniDrip has been rigorously tested and validated over simulations, demonstrating its dependability in real-world situations, and demonstrating its potential to revolutionize saline infusion management. This research paper provides an overview of the development, implementation, and assessment of this system, which has the potential to revolutionize healthcare practices by providing uninterrupted and continuous saline infusion. By incorporating advanced monitoring technology and intelligent alerts, this system has the potential to significantly improve patient care and streamline medical procedures.

articleTitle: Development of SFCW Based GPR for Sub-Surface Scanning
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is a non destructive geophysical technique that uses electromagnetic waves to image the subsurface. GPR has a wide range of applications including archaeological survey, landmine and tunnel detection, glacier analysis, and many more. However, GPR systems are limited by their resolution and sensitivity. Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave (SFCW) radar is a promising technique for subsurface scanning due to its high resolution and sensitivity. SFCW radar systems are complex and require significant processing to extract important and meaningful information from received signals. This paper proposes a novel SFCW radar system based on GNU Radio and MATLAB for subsurface scanning with intelligent classification algorithms. The proposed system uses a stepped frequency waveform to achieve high resolution and employs intelligent classification algorithms to identify and classify the subsurface targets. The system is implemented using GNU Radio and MATLAB, and its performance is evaluated using simulated and real-world data. The simulated data are generated using a subsurface scattering model, while the real world data are collected from a subsurface test bed. The results demonstrate that the proposed system can effectively identify and accurately classify subsurface targets.

articleTitle: Combining Deep Features with the Invariant Local Binary Pattern features for Skin Cancer Classification
abstract: Melanoma, a potentially fatal form of skin cancer, represents a global health concern, necessitating efficient and precise detection for improved patient outcomes. However, the subjective and daunting nature of manual examination and diagnosing skin lesions by dermatologists often leads to delayed identification or misdiagnosis. This research paper introduces a novel technique for automated melanoma classification to address this pressing problem. The proposed research methodology combines deep features with rotation-invariant handcrafted local-binary pattern (RI-LBP) features for skin lesion classification. RI-LBP extracts microstructures present at the local level whereas deep features capture the high-level intuitive features present in a skin lesion image. After combining RI-LBP with the deep features, the combined feature vector is used to train and test the XGBoost machine learning classifier for classification purposes. Moreover, the investigation undertakes a comparative analysis of numerous machine learning algorithms to evaluate their efficacy in the classification of melanoma using the suggested combined feature set. The XGBoost classifier has obtained an Area Under the Curve value of 0.91 in differentiating pernicious melanomas and benign skin lesion dermoscopic images. Thus, the proposed method is suitable for aiding dermatologists, enhancing the efficacy and precision of melanoma identification and treatment, and ultimately yielding superior patient care and outcomes.

articleTitle: An Effective Checkerboard Calibration Technique for a Stereo Camera System
abstract: One of the most important abilities of the human vision system is the capacity to perceive the environment in three dimensions. Due to the spatial separation between the two eyes in the horizontal direction, the two images produced in the two eyes are different from one another. These results served as the basis for in-depth investigation into the extraction of depth from two or more images taken from the same scene from varied angles, giving the impression of three-dimensional shapes. The three-dimensional space is approximated by calculating the pixel difference between the two stereo pictures taken from reality. This research describes a framework for creating a disparity map and depth map in order to minimize or reduce the issues that are now present. Multiple cameras are becoming more common in mobile devices, and these stereo pictures may be utilised for depth sensing. However, because they frequently contain a variety of attributes, such as resolutions, deviations, and fields of view, using the raw images from the cameras is difficult. As part of this study, we propose and evaluate techniques for quickly and easily acquiring stereo images from several cameras in a matter of 0.346 seconds.

articleTitle: Comparison of Interpolation Scaling Algorithm and Efficient VLSI Design of Win-Scale Interpolation for Run Time Digital Picture Spreading
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital display sizes, the clarity of digital image demonstration has increased. Although the computational cost of the win-scale algorithm prevents it from processing in real-time. In this study, we put the win-scale algorithm into an effective VLSI architecture design. This method is suited for digital image display in a range of various sharpness of the image. The Correspondence calculator register, the picture element adjustment unit, the dimension calculation unit, and the accumulating unit make up the heart of the system. The successful development of the speedy VLSI architectonics has been built using our method. The simulation findings show that digital picture spreading for HDTV can be processed in run time by the high-performance image scaling architecture running at frequency 128.37MHz with 18763 total gates in 450x450 micrometer square main size of the wafer.

articleTitle: An Appropriate Histogram Equalization Technique for Thermal Image Enhancement of Neck Region
abstract: The pattern of heat distribution in the human body is a natural and early indicator of anomalies. A noninvasive screening method for determining body temperature distribution is thermal imaging. The distribution of an object's thermal radiation can be seen in thermal images. However, the infrared images typically have little contrast. As a result, it is important to increase the contrast of IR images before they are recognized and analyzed. In this research, more effective approaches for increasing the quality of infrared thermal images are presented. This study investigates different Histogram Equalization techniques - Adaptive Histogram Equalization, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization and Adaptive double plateaus histogram equalization to improve the gray scale contrast of the thermal Image. For our experiment, we have used 12 thermal images of the thyroid for AHE, CLAHE and ADPHE processing. After preprocessing and post processing of IR images, statistical parameters are derived. Processing on thermal images used in this work suggest the best HE approach which generates greater contrast-enhancement results for thermal images with extra information.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Prediction Using Various Machine Learning Algorithms and Their Comparative Analysis
abstract: Breast cancer is a grave health risk and impacts millions of women globally. For effective treatment, it must be detected as early as possible. Use of ML-based algorithms for the breast cancer prediction is becoming widespread. Machine learning algorithms are well-suited for such applications as they can analyze vast amounts of data and have the ability to spot intricate patterns in it. In this paper, breast cancer prediction is done using various ML algorithms including Support Vector Machine (Linear, Polynomial and Radial), Boosted tree, Logistic Regression and Random Forest. Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) dataset has been selected for training and testing purpose. The prediction models have been compared using various performance parameters observed. Results indicate that these prediction models are effective in breast cancer prediction.

articleTitle: Face Database Protection Using Encryption Technique
abstract: Biometric is being extensively used for security applications. The major concern with biometric features is, there are limited features for a single person. Compromise of these features will lead to compromising of security and it will be impossible to replace these features as they are unique to every person. For securing biometric database various methods have been proposed like cancelable biometric and biometric cryptosystem. The issues arising from these are matching template in transform domain, authenticity etc. To overcome this problem, encryption-based method is proposed for database present in the server. The transfer of database from server to terminal for authentication is done in encrypted domain along with storage. For authentication, the database is decrypted at the terminal side. The cipher output and security parameters shown in the paper verifies that the algorithm is successful in securing facial database.

articleTitle: Peti-Chain – Blockchain Based Judicial Petition Filing System
abstract: The Petition-filing process in the Indian Judicial System is an integral part of the Indian Judiciary. The digital process of petition filing is very slow and cumbersome. Moreover, it is just dependent on the central system. This makes the overall system very vulnerable in terms of digital security and preservation of old records. This problem can be solved by making the whole system decentralized. By making use of the Blockchain technology, the petition-filing system would become more secure and easier to access. This process would also help the overall system by making the whole petition-filing process faster, for both the courts and the petition-filers. In this paper, we present a unique way of implementing the use of decentralized blockchain systems in the context of digital petition-filing.

articleTitle: Data-driven Insights into Snake-bite Incidents: A Visual Analysis Approach
abstract: As per World Health Organisation Report, more than one lakh people die yearly from snake bites. Many people survive the snake bite affected by partial or complete disability. India snake-bite data shows more than 1.2 billion deaths estimated between the period 2000 to 2019. The probability of snake-bite is likely to be more in rural areas. Awareness of the snake-bite management guidelines can lead to a reduction in snake-bite cases. Timely treatment of the victim can significantly reduce the death rate due to snake-bite circumstances. Snakebite is one of the issues in human-wildlife conflict. People tend to kill the snake out of fear without trying to verify whether the snake is venomous or non-venomous. The research paper aims to study the patterns of snake-bite cases reported in different states in India. This analysis can give insights into the demand for anti-snake venom in various states in India. The methodology adopted is exploratory research using secondary data available on India Stat for snake bite cases between the period 2012-2021 in 35 states and territories in India. The researcher has done the pattern analysis in snake-bite cases using computer tools and techniques like Python Programming and Tableau Desktop.

articleTitle: Non Invasive Approach for Dental Caries Detection
abstract: In developing nation like India, dental health is highly ignored health domain. This is due to the lack of awareness, lack of education, socio-economic background and poverty. Hence an automated system of dental caries detection is necessary which will reduce the burden on dental practitioners. The presented system focuses on dental caries detection using convolutional neural network with four layers of convolution. Web based database of 74 single tooth digital RGB images are used for the study. 60 images were used for training and 14 were used for testing. Data augmentation is done since the database is low. System with three convolution layers have been implemented initially. The results are compared. With three convolution and pooling layers 78.57% accuracy is obtained whereas with four layers of convolution and pooling layers 85.71% accuracy is obtained. This model gives the platform for future research in the dental disease's detection using deep learning approaches using multiclass classification.

articleTitle: Home Automation System using Internet-of-Things & Blynk App
abstract: In recent times, human intervention has been significantly reduced with the help of Internet-of-Things devices. A better monitoring control and faster response is received with the help of this technology. Human machine interaction is increasing continuously and Internet-of-Things is a step ahead by connecting the smart objects with the internet and therefore making overall working easier. In this work, a cost effective, energy efficient and flexible design of home automation is proposed which connects and controls various home appliances using NodeMCU, Google assistance and Blynk app. It provides a helping hand for the old aged and for differently abled persons. Human intervention is significantly reduced and in case of emergencies it has detecting capabilities which make it more reliable. User friendliness is provided through Google Assistant using voice commands. Blynk application helps to connect through an app and by using IFTTT, user can create a customised command for each job for Google Assistant. Proposed design also take care of the gas, temperature and humidity of the house using DHT11; the temperature and humidity sensor and MQ02; which is a gas sensor. Values of these sensors are displayed in the application which is connected to the relay. NodeMCU has been used for connecting Blynk app. Blynk server has been configured with NodeMCU using authentication key and further Blynk server is connected to the webhooks server which acts as a broker. For connecting Google Assistant, IFTTT has been used using IF-THEN conditions.

articleTitle: Design and IoT Implementation of a LiDAR Assisted Large-Area Video Surveillance Network
abstract: Over the years, the advancement of technology has evolved the surveillance system to a new dimension in comparison with the age-old approach, which is highly human-dependent from multiple aspects, such as patrolling, tracking a suspect, monitoring, and so on. As the modernization of the surveillance system makes it more sophisticated, on the downside, it imposes several technical challenges, like maintenance cost, scalability of the network, and others. In this paper, we have tried to address a few of those challenges to make the surveillance system more efficient. The proposed design of a multi-sensor data fusion, along with the transfer learning and the implementation of the Long Range (LoRa) technology based Internet-of-Things (IoT) framework, provides an efficient system with some degree of scalability. As the multiple sensors are utilized, the storage consumption has reduced significantly along with the computational cost. In addition to that, transfer learning method based video analysis has enhanced its efficiency, which reduces the human effort for monitoring. Lastly, the LoRa based IoT framework allows us to cover a large geographical area with a provision of scaling up the whole architecture as per the requirement. Nevertheless, the overall performance of this proposed framework has been evaluated, and it yields highly accurate performance in different scenarios.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-Based Visual Detection of Road Hazards: Potholes, Sewer Covers, and Manholes
abstract: Effective detection of road hazards plays a pivotal role in road infrastructure maintenance and ensuring road safety. This research paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of YOLOv8, an object detection model, in the context of detecting road hazards such as potholes, sewer covers, and manHoles. A comparative analysis with previous iterations, YOLOv5 and YOLOv7, is conducted, emphasizing the importance of compu-tational efficiency in various applications. The paper delves into the architecture of YOLOv8 and explores image preprocessing techniques aimed at enhancing detection accuracy across diverse conditions, including variations in lighting, road types, hazard sizes, and types. Furthermore, hyperparameter tuning experiments are performed to optimize model performance through adjustments in learning rates, batch sizes, anchor box sizes, and augmentation strategies. Model evaluation is based on Mean Average Precision (mAP), a widely accepted metric for object detection performance. The research assesses the robustness and generalization capabilities of the models through mAP scores calculated across the diverse test scenarios, underlining the sig-nificance of YOLOv8 in road hazard detection and infrastructure maintenance.

articleTitle: Xavier Vision: Pioneering Autonomous Vehicle Perception with YOLO v8 on Jetson Xavier NX
abstract: The real-time detection and identification of objects is critical to the efficient and safe navigation of autonomous vehicles (AVs). It is the initial phase of developing autonomous vehicles. Using low-power, tiny processing units along with edge computing has shown promise for object detection in autonomous vehicles. In this article, we look at and talk about the advantages and disadvantages of using the Jetson Xavier NX board for object detection in autonomous vehicles. We provide a synopsis of the most sophisticated deep learning model for object detection, called YOLO v8, discuss whether it can be used with the Jetson board, and investigate the next steps for integrating the two for edge computing. According to research, Jetson Xavier can effectively use the YOLO v8 with a mAP of up to 93%, an F1 score of 89.29%, and a response time as low as 6.7 ms. To solve the issues and guarantee the safe and responsible deployment of autonomous cars with object detection capabilities, more research and development is necessary.

articleTitle: ML Powered Analytics for Sensing Demand in Consumer Industry
abstract: The consumer goods industry is facing significant challenges in meeting the consumer's everevolving demands and preferences. The e-commerce and online delivery brought in the ease of access to purchase products, while the popularity of social media brought the social sentiment angle which are impacting customer purchases patterns. These factors are leading to a rise in influencer marketing campaigns and have enabled businesses or brands to reach consumers faster. The goal of the study is to address these challenges and to explore the use of Machine learning and big data analytic techniques to provide insights by understanding consumer purchase patterns, sales data, market and social media trends, news feed and stock levels to predict future demand for products in advance which will better enable inventory planning.

articleTitle: Exploring the Efficacy of Partial Denoising Using Bit Plane Slicing for Enhanced Fracture Identification: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning-Based Approaches and Handcrafted Feature Extraction Techniques
abstract: Computer vision has transformed medical diagnosis, treatment, and research through advanced image processing and machine learning techniques. Fracture classification, a critical area in healthcare, has greatly benefited from these advancements, yet accurate detection is challenged by complex patterns and image noise. Bit plane slicing enhances medical images by reducing noise interference and extracting informative features. This research explores partial denoising techniques to provide practical solutions for improved fracture analysis, ultimately enhancing patient care. The study explores deep learning model DenseNet, and handcrafted feature extraction. Decision Tree and Random Forest, were employed to train and evaluate distinct image representations. These include the original image, the concatenation of the four bit planes from the LSB, the four bit planes from the MSB, the fully denoised image, and an image consisting of six bit planes from MSB and two denoised bit planes from LSB. The purpose of forming these diverse image representations is to analyze SNR as well as classification accuracy and identify the bit planes that contain the most informative features. Moreover, the study delves into the significance of partial denoising techniques in preserving crucial features, leading to improvements in classification results. Notably, this study shows that employing the Random Forest classifier, the partially denoised image representation exhibited a testing accuracy of 95.61%, surpassing the performance of other image representations. These numerical results underscore the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately identifying fractures. The outcomes of this research provide valuable insights into the development of efficient preprocessing, feature extraction and classification approaches for fracture identification. By enhancing diagnostic accuracy, these advancements hold the potential to positively impact patient care and overall medical outcomes.

articleTitle: Development of Firm Security Plan for IoT with Continual Learning Algorithms
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of interconnected devices that may be used to remotely detect, identify, and operate physical objects. IoT's qualities allow for the incorporation of the real world into a digital system, which improves precision, productivity, and bottom-line results. The old internet is made up of powerful computers and servers with a wide range of resources, whereas IoT devices have less computing time and memory. The complicated security protocols and several layers used in conventional networks are incompatible with the real-time nature of the Internet of Things. The adoption of IoT devices in several contexts has raised serious concerns about users' privacy and safety, leading to a meteoric rise in the prevalence of cyber-attacks. The larger a network becomes, the more likely it is to be attacked. Therefore, the IoT network is far more susceptible to attacks than conventional networks. Since the number of potential attackers in an IoT setting is growing exponentially, so too are the security risks. To protect the IoT ecosystem from current threats, cutting-edge technology is essential. The suggested resampling approach, CLA-ST (Sampling Technique), is based on the Random Forest Synthetic Minority Over Sampling Technique. To identify risks in the IoT ecosystem, we use the CLA-ST, which is based on a network search calculation improvement approach. Proposed study conducts experiments on the N-BaIoT dataset and the NSL-KDD dataset to evaluate attack recognition in the IoT. There must be a reliable mechanism in place to detect and prevent threats in the IoT ecosystem. When compared to PPDT-ST, the suggested technique outperforms it in both attack detection and categorization.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Different Pre-Processing Pipelines for EEG-Based Preference Prediction in Neuromarketing
abstract: Neuromarketing is an emerging brain-computer interface (BCI) research field that aims to understand consumers' internal decision-making processes when choosing which products to buy. It provides valuable insights for marketers to improve their marketing strategies based on consumers' impressions. However, the current status of Electroencephalography (EEG)-based preference prediction and its classification accuracy is still below optimal. The performance of an EEG-based preference prediction system largely depends on the suitable selection of a proper EEG preprocessing pipeline since noisy EEG data is likely not to give better results. Most of the studies followed a traditional EEG pre-processing pipeline and also recently an advanced automated EEG pre-processing pipeline has been introduced in the literature. In this study, we have proposed an optimal EEG pre-processing pipeline and compared it with the other two methods mentioned above. We collected raw EEG data and pre-processed them using the three pre-processing pipelines. We then extracted many statistical and frequency domain features and employed several machine-learning classification models. After implementing our proposed pipeline to preprocess EEG data, we observed a significant improvement in classification accuracies. Specifically, our pipeline achieved 100% accuracy for Ensemble learning, and 93.3% accuracy for k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN) model. In comparison, for the same classifiers the traditional and advanced automated pipelines achieved 75%, 83.3%, and 78.3%, 87% accuracies respectively.

articleTitle: Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network Model for Crop Disease Identification using UAV Imagery
abstract: With the rising growth in population, the need for food production is increasing day by day. This fosters the need for sustainable food production. However, agricultural products are majorly hampered by diseases on crops. To handle such diseases, automated crop disease identification systems can play a pivotal role. This study attempts to provide a comprehensive exploration of the application of geo-intelligent techniques for automated disease identification. The study presents Northern Leaf blight (NLB) disease recognition in Maize crops using advanced deep-learning techniques applied on high-resolution maize crop leaf imagery obtained through UAVs. Deep learning techniques involving sequential model and transfer learning approaches were explored on high-resolution imagery to classify maize leaves into diseased and healthy categories. It is observed that transfer learning models like Xception performed well in comparison with other models for precise disease identification. Additionally, the study has also explored the potential of YOLOv8 which demonstrates minimal loss with comparable performance. An accuracy of 81.1%, 80.7%, 80.3%, 78.9%, 78.8%, and 75.9% is observed using Xception, CNN, ResNet50, NASNet Mobile, VGG16, and YOLOv8, respectively. This study contributes valuable insights into automated NLB recognition and also holds implications for revolutionizing disease detection across the broader landscape of Indian agriculture. The utilization of advanced deep-learning methodologies offers a promising avenue for safeguarding crop health and enhancing food security in the nation.

articleTitle: XAI Meets Ophthalmology: An Explainable Approach to Cataract Detection Using VGG-19 and Grad-CAM
abstract: Cataract is the most common cause of blindness in the world, and early detection is critical for successful treatment. Deep learning algorithms have recently demonstrated promising results in automated cataract detection from fundus images. Yet, the inability of these black box models to be interpreted raises concerns regarding their clinical application. In this paper, we present an explainable approach for detecting cataracts using the VGG-19 convolutional neural network (CNN) and the Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) visualization technique. We trained and tested our model using 2,112 high-resolution fundus images from a publicly available dataset. According to our findings, the proposed method obtains a very high accuracy of 97%. Furthermore, the Grad-CAM visuals show the image regions that contribute to the model's decision, providing insights into the diagnosis process and increasing the model's trustworthiness. The findings of this study could assist in improving patient outcomes and lowering healthcare costs by allowing for the early detection and diagnosis of cataracts. Overall, the combination of VGG-19 with Grad-CAM offers a viable option in the medical domain for identifying cataracts and understanding CNN - based decisions.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Object Dimension Estimation System
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for real-time object dimension estimation systems. In order to create a trustworthy dimension detection system and investigate its applicability in many sectors, this study provides a novel approach for real-time object dimension estimation systems. In numerous disciplines, including manufacturing and engineering, architecture and construction, robotics and automation, augmented reality, and many others, the precise estimation of item dimensions is a crucial component. In this model, the realtime size feature is computed using the YoloV5 model. The proposed system is implemented on the Jetson. Nano-embedded development system. A custom dataset of 2400 images of each of the three classes (bottle, cup, and grocery bag) is used in the training of models. The detection and localization are performed using YoloV5. Recognition and identifying the images are done by Convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithms. The bounding box coordinates are used to estimate an object's size from a distance of 75 cm from the camera by using the Linear Regression method. The accuracy of the system's detection of the bottle, cup, and grocery bag is 88%, 84%, and 87%, respectively. The object dimension estimation has observed close to -0.1/ +0.1cm variation and presented a justified approach for the difference in accuracy evaluation of the detection and size estimation model.

articleTitle: Impact of Electric Vehicles on DISCOM: A Vision to Get Prepared for the Future
abstract: This paper examines the impact of Electric Vehicles (EVs) on distribution companies (DISCOMs) and the grid, focusing on projections for the year 2030. Data from the Maharashtra State Load Dispatch Center's monthly reports and Western Regional Load Despatch Centre's (WRLDC) annual reports detailing peak and minimum demand, as well as overall energy consumption, form the basis of this analysis. Employing a de-seasonalised trend forecasting method, the study predicts energy requirements for 2030, with the reapplication of seasonal variations for accuracy. Battery specifications for various EV types, including two-wheelers, three-wheelers, four-wheelers, and buses, were gathered from manufacturers' websites to calculate average battery sizes. The study examines the impact of EV adoption at three different market penetration levels - 10, 20, and 30 percent by 2030 - on energy demand. Findings suggest that these adoption rates could lead to a variation in energy demand, ranging from a decrease of up to 12 percent to an increase of up to 15 percent compared to projected requirements for that year. This research provides essential insights for DISCOMs to strategically plan for the expected increase in electricity demand due to the growing prevalence of EVs.

articleTitle: Explainable AI for Reliable Detection of Cyberbullying
abstract: The advent of Internet has brought a pivotal revolution in communication technology. This revolution is observed through tremendous use of devices like cell phones and social networking websites that provide a platform for people to interact virtually. The use of social networking websites has provided economical, educational and societal benefits. The ease of access to information and the liberty to openly share and publish information on social networking sites also has a downside. Past decade has witnessed an upsurge of objectionable and cyberbullying content shared on social media. The massiveness and the sensitive bullying content shared on social media platforms make manual method of detecting such content practically challenging. Automated approaches like Artificial Intelligence (AI) based techniques are widely being adopted to detect and moderate online cyberbullying content.
