Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Deep Learning (DL) are at forefront in automating the detection of cyberbullying content. Inspite of the wide adoption of DL models for detection of bullying content, the decision and predictions made by these models are difficult to comprehend. Explainable AI (XAI) is a promising field that provide interpretations to the decision made by DL models. Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) XAI technique provide better explanations by highlighting the most pertinent features that contributed to model's decision. This paper proposes a unified BiLSTM-LIME model for multiclass classification of cyberbullying content on Twitter platform.

articleTitle: A Systematic Literature Review of Classical and Quantum Machine Learning Approaches for Mutual Fund Portfolio Optimization
abstract: Quantum Computing is a dynamic field which has evolved since its inception around 3 decades back, to the development of various powerful algorithms including Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) to name a few. Today's quantum computers are not as powerful as the current breed of supercomputers. However, the existing breed of NISQ (Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum) quantum computers have a significant potential to provide faster solutions to problems in various domains which are not just relevant for the present but also for the future such as Quantum Machine Learning in the Fintech domain. Portfolio Optimization (PO) is one such problem in research and the financial services industry at large. In principle, Quantum Computing, makes it possible to arrive at an optimal portfolio composition for a high return and low risk investment much faster than any existing supercomputer today. This review paper examines literature on classical and quantum machine learning approaches for Mutual Fund PO, analyzing 44 papers from 2003 to 2023. PO being a vast topic, we limit our scope to Mutual Funds and its driver that is the equity markets. We provide an overview to the types of problems, preferred approaches, their benchmarks, deduced conclusions, and research gaps as a comprehensive survey for diverse readers.

articleTitle: Magnetostrictive Sensor Based Bridge Health Assessment Using Machine Learning Classifiers
abstract: Bridge Health Monitoring (BHM) is a crucial research domain in engineering, involving the analysis of infrastructure conditions like bridges using sensor data. Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) systems comprise distinct phases, with pivotal stages being feature extraction and pattern recognition. Signal processing techniques aid in feature extraction, while Machine Learning algorithms play a crucial role in pattern recognition, all geared towards accurately assessing bridge health. Applying Machine Learning techniques permits the automation of the SHM procedure and intelligent damage detection. This study introduces an innovative method utilizing Machine Learning technologies, leveraging data from Galfenol-based Magnetostrictive Sensors. These sensors convert vibrations into electrical data, offering insights into bridge health. A Decision Tree classifier categorizes data with an 80:20 split for training and testing, achieving a 98.72% accuracy. The code also demonstrates its predictive capability with new experimental data. Furthermore, various classifiers, including the Support Vector Method (SVM) and Neural Network, are tested, revealing their comparable accuracy. This research provides a user-friendly avenue for SHM and assists researchers in selecting optimal classification methods.

articleTitle: Metaverse and Students Engagement – Instructors' Perspective
abstract: The paper explores how metaverse helps in engaging students in virtual education in higher education institutions (HEIs). It also tries to analyze the drivers and challenges for acceptance of Metaverse in online education. The research involved in-depth-interviews of 15 respondents who were instructors in institutions in reputed cities in the USA. Teacher who had taught virtually for at least 5 years were selected through purposive sampling for this study. Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) technique was applied for detailed analysis of the responses received from teachers. The research reveals that Metaverse could be used as an attractive immersive platform in virtual education. However, the instructors need to apply it constructively, aligning it with the course they teach and the pedagogy they apply. The research will be useful to HEIs and instructors who can design customized metaverse platforms to suit their online courses. The research will guide global companies operating in the metaverse domain to improvise their designs for a potential online education sector. The research will enhance the quality of virtual education and reduce dropout rate of students. It will make online education sector more inclusive, engaging and thereby lucrative for students. The study is original and novel in the area of online education sector. The study will be useful to policy makers in the higher education sector and government institutions in understanding the potential use of Metaverse in online education.

articleTitle: Leveraging Data Science for Mitigating GNSS Multipath and Signal Interference in IoT Devices
abstract: The integration of IoT devices with GNSS technology has revolutionized location-based services and applications, offering diverse possibilities. However, GNSS multipath and signal interference problems commonly affect these devices, leading to compromised location dependability and accuracy. This study explores the problems with GNSS multipath and signal interference in IoT devices and offers viable fixes. The objectives of this study were: i) Conduct a comprehensive analysis of the causes and effects of GNSS multipath and signal interference in IoT devices. ii) Evaluate the current methodologies and approaches employed for mitigating GNSS multipath and signal interference. iii) Propose a novel multipath and interference mitigation technique which can enhance GNSS positioning and robustness of IoT devices. The study results discussed in this article promote IoT-enabled location-based services and give practitioners and researchers working in the field of GNSS and IoT integration invaluable insights.

articleTitle: Exploring the Horizons of Speaker Recognition: Contemporary Advancements and Prospective Trajectories in the Age of Deep Learning
abstract: Speaker recognition is a prominent area of study within speech technology. In recent times, there has been a notable transition towards embedding-based end-to-end speaker recognition approaches. These methods enable speaker recognition without the need for retraining when encountering new speakers in real-world scenarios. Earlier models were trained on limited monotonous hand-crafted datasets, which worked on pattern matching, but failed to be robust because of architectural limitations and insufficient data. Research shows that training deep neural networks, which rely on attention mechanisms, on extensive datasets containing weakly labeled and diverse samples can significantly improve their resilience when applied to various classification tasks downstream. Drawing upon knowledge acquired from extensive datasets like VoxCelebl and VoxCeleb2, along with specially crafted proprietary data tailored to handle various modalities, we initiated an investigation into the capabilities of these versatile techniques for building speaker recognition models. Our attention was directed towards two reputable models, ECAPA-TDNN [1](Emphasized Channel Attention, Propagation, and Aggregation) and Titanet[2], as we aimed to comprehend the architectural enhancements and assess their impact on the model's ability to generalize effectively. Also, we propose a faster and scalable inference pipeline using Elasticsearch.

articleTitle: SPECTER-Based Transformer Model For Multi-Label Research Paper Classification
abstract: The ever-increasing number of research and academia publications presents new problems for future researchers and publication libraries, such as difficulty finding the proper papers for literature reviews due to cluttered data and inadequate keywords. It also hinders academic libraries from creating adequate indexing and leads to more and more unstructured data. This paper proposes a novel solution for classifying published research and scholarly articles, which would help solve the given problems by facilitating improved search engine optimization for online academic libraries. The study method utilizes the openly available arXiv dataset of 2.3 million records containing the metadata for each published research paper, which includes the title and the abstract. It uses the paper's metadata as the input and outputs multiple labels related to the input domain. The research compared different techniques for multi-label classification tasks and proposed a Specter method, which uses a transformer-based model for the task of research article classification. This method achieved a significant increase in precision and accuracy on the dataset and will help improve the maintenance of scholarly articles and make relevant works more readily available.

articleTitle: Medical Assistance for Detecting Cataract, Jaundice and Strabismus using Deep Learning
abstract: Eye diseases are prevailing either due to poor diet, unhealthy lifestyle, hereditary factors or pre-term birth. Many people are unable to get adequate access to trained medical professionals and proper healthcare infrastructure. Often, the eye ailments remain undetected in the early stages, when taking proper prescriptions and precautions can prevent any further serious health issues. This paper proposes a medical diagnosis system for the automatic machine analysis of eye conditions including cataract, jaundice, and strabismus, along with a potent chatbot developed using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques for and effective medical assistance. In cataract patients, the eye lens gets cloudy and hinders the proper vision. Jaundice is a liver disease, symptoms of which include yellowish eye. Strabismus is another eye condition when both eyes are not aligned symmetrically when focusing on any visual. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models are developed and designed to attained an accuracy of 99.31%, 99.77% and 97.82% for detecting cataract, jaundice and strabismus respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of Uday Scheme in Improving Financial Health of Indian Power Distribution Companies Pre Covid-19
abstract: The study aims to find significant initiatives taken under the UDAY scheme and analyze its efficiency in improving the financial performance and initiatives having a major contribution in improving revenue and profit generations of five Indian state DISCOMs. The collection and analysis of pre-COVID-19 financial data by state DISCOMs and the primary analysis were made from the information available on the UDAY portal, offering aggregate and state output information on the 14 different parameters. The five state DISCOMs were selected on the basis of their current annual rating by the Ministry of Power so that the study can be performed for different rated DISCOMs to understand holistic results. The financial criteria examined were a reduction in AT&C losses, a gap between the average power supply cost/unit, and the average realization of revenue per unit (ACS-ARR). Analysis was performed to identify the parameters with a significant impact on improving efficiency for each DISCOM. The findings suggest that initiatives under the UDAY scheme helped in improving five DISCOMs' financial performance, AT&C losses level, and ACS-ARR gap.

articleTitle: Enhancing Malicious Domain Detection Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: The necessity of comprehensive cybersecurity measures cannot be emphasized in today's quickly expanding digital world. Due to the rising complexity and frequency of cyber attacks, detecting malicious domains has become an urgent problem. Conventional methods often struggle to accurately identify sophisticated attacks, highlighting the need for innovative solutions. This research aims to address the urgent issue of detecting malicious domains by introducing a novel approach that harnesses the strengths of both the HistGradientBoosting-Classifier and Artificial Neural Networks. Through the synergistic combination of diverse algorithms, we propose a solution that has the potential to redefine cybersecurity, enhancing both accuracy and effectiveness. It is crucial to emphasize the significance of this problem within the current cybersecurity landscape, where threat actors continuously adapt their tactics to exploit vulnerabilities. Our study involves the meticulous curation of a dataset, enriched with essential features, showcasing substantial progress in enhancing detection accuracy. Through rigorous comparative analysis, we establish that the integration of various machine learning algorithms and domain name system features has the potential to revolutionize malicious domain detection. The implications of these findings extend well beyond the realm of academic research and hold a profound impact on practical cybersecurity. The incorporation of the Histogram Gradient Boosting Classifier and Artificial Neural Network represents a forward-thinking approach that can proactively address emerging challenges. By integrating these machine learning-driven insights into cyber-security strategies, organizations can significantly bolster their capabilities in safezuardina diaital infrastructures.

articleTitle: Harnessing Deep Learning for Tea Tree Leaf Disease Management: A CNN-SVM Perspective
abstract: The health and yield of the crops are affected, which presents serious problems for the tea business. Effective disease control and long-term tea production depend on early and precise disease identification. Anthracnose, blister blight, red rust, grey blight, brown blight, and orange spot are six prevalent diseases that affect tea tree leaves. In this study, the researchers suggest a unique method employing convolutional neural networks and support vector machines to forecast these illnesses. Precision, recall, F1-Score, support, as well as accuracy indicators, are used to assess the model's effectiveness. The CNN-SVM model distinguishes out with a remarkable 95.01 percent overall accuracy. The accuracy, recall, and F1-Score values, which range between 92.06% to 96.49%, further demonstrate the model's capacity to correctly identify diseases inflicting tea tree leaves. The study's conclusions highlight the model's potential as a trustworthy tool for tea farmers to identify and control infections, eventually assisting in the development of sustainable teagrowing practices. Future studies may concentrate on improving the model further and investigating new data augmentation strategies to improve its illness-detection skills.

articleTitle: Adult Autism Screening and Prediction using Ensemble Approach
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder is a neuro developmental disorder that affects communication and behavior. Although ASD is typically diagnosed in childhood, it can also be diagnosed in adulthood. However, adults with ASD are often underdiagnosed, which can lead to a number of challenges, such as social isolation, employment difficulties and mental health problems. Early diagnosis and intervention can make a significant difference in the lives of autistic people. With appropriate support, autistic people can thrive in school work and their personal lives. However, without a diagnosis, autistic people may not be able to access the services and support they need. Approximately half of adults with ASD (autism spectrum disorder) may remain undiagnosed due to reasons like limited awareness among healthcare providers, the stigma linked to ASD and the variation in how ASD demonstrates in adults compared to children. This research paper explores the crucial role of machine learning algorithms on screening of Autism in adults. The paper provides an introduction to the topic followed by a methodology section detailing the various algorithms used. This survey paper provides the comparative analysis of different machine learning algorithms for Autism screening through different models such as DecisionTreeClassifier, GaussianNB, RandomForestClassifier. This study assessed the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms: DecisionTreeClassifier, GaussianNB and RandomForestClassifier. GaussianNB demonstrated the best performance with an accuracy of 85.85%. Finally, the paper concludes by highlighting the significance of machine learning algorithms in improving disorder detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Identification and Mitigation of Unintentional Insider Information Leak Threats in Public Repositories
abstract: Software vulnerabilities on public repositories such as GitHub pose a serious threat to software project development, compromising system availability, data integrity, and confidentiality. This work addresses the need for high-quality software development and effective cybersecurity practices by introducing CredStroller, a tool designed to passively identify potential vulnerabilities in public GitHub repositories. CredStroller offers a unique advantage over scanning tools in that it can scan source code using regular expression patterns across many large numbers of repositories, including those not related to the organization. This capability helps identify mistakes made by developers when they inadvertently upload sensitive source code to their personal GitHub accounts, which are not managed by the organization. The development of a Chrome plugin for CredStroller was motivated by the ease of use and the quick and easy visual identification of secrets it provides. By providing greater accuracy and data coverage for vulnerability detection, CredStroller presents a significant contribution to improving cybersecurity practices. This paper highlights the approach and procedures used to create the Chrome plugin tool and presents results from testing the tool, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying vulnerabilities. The conclusion summarizes the key findings and highlights the contributions of this work towards achieving that goal.

articleTitle: Advanced Face Authentication Using Deep Learning Models
abstract: This paper conducts a comprehensive study and evaluation of various face recognition models, aiming to provide valuable insights for face recognition tasks. The models under investigation include VGGFace(ResNet50), Dlib with KNN, Siamese Network, FaceNet, and Dlib with OpenCV. Each model undergoes a meticulous assessment in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. The research commences with an exploration of VGGFace(ResNet50), a deep-learning model fine-tuned on a custom data set to evaluate its performance under diverse conditions. Next, the study delves into Dlib with KNN, lever-aging Dlib's capabilities for face detection, landmark detection, and encoding, combined with the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm for classification. The Siamese Network architecture is also investigated to address one-shot learning challenges, followed by an evaluation of FaceN et's highly discriminating face embedding. Finally, the integrated approach combining Dlib and OpenCV libraries for real-time face recognition is thoroughly analyzed and implemented. The findings offer crucial insights into the strengths, limitations, and applicability of each model, facilitating informed decision-making for specific face recognition applications. By combining multiple of these models, a robust FR model is built having an accuracy of more than 90 % which will play a significant role in the computer vision domain.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Inference Attacks in Federated Learning
abstract: In the face of increasing data silos and mounting privacy concerns, the traditional centralized method of training machine learning models encounters significant obstacles. Federated Learning has emerged as a compelling solution in this evolving environment. However, the existing Federated Learning protocols have demonstrated vulnerabilities that adversaries can exploit, jeopardizing data privacy. This paper investigates the implications of various attacks on federated learning. We explore the impact of these attacks, considering the decentralized nature of Federated Learning and its susceptibility to privacy breaches. Additionally, we offer detailed implementations of the inference attacks and propose strategies to mitigate the potential risks, thus enhancing the overall privacy and security of the Federated Learning framework.

articleTitle: Detecting Mental Health Disorders Using NLP
abstract: The concept of mental fitness pertains to the state of possessing a sound and adaptable mind, characterized by good health and resilience. It encompasses the capacity to navigate challenges and setbacks in a constructive and flexible manner. Consequently, the cultivation and sustenance of mental fitness contribute significantly to the improvement of individual well-being and overall quality of life. In 2019, the WHO observation showed that close to a billion people around the world were living with a mental disorder especially depression and anxiety being the most common. There are various NLP projects which deal with classifying a specific mental health disorder based on analysis of text or speech but very few deal with multi-level classification. To address this we are doing a single model with multilevel mental health disorder classification-combining the text data from many data sets of individual classes. To address this we are creating a composite framework with multilevel mental health disorder classification-combining the text data of different classes from a dataset of reddit posts. Our experiments have shown that fine-tuned domain-specific transformer models and hybrid models combining transformer models and recurrent neural network models like LSTM and Bi-LSTM can detect mental health disorder with an fl-score of 88 % and above.

articleTitle: Unveiling Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection: A Comprehensive Study of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
abstract: According to research by the world health organization (WHO), approximately 0.63% of children are diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). ASD commonly emerges during childhood and persists through adolescence and adulthood. Early detection of ASD is crucial as it can lead to effective interventions and improved outcomes. Machine learning and deep learning techniques have gained significant recognition for their efficacy in various fields including biomedicine and medicine. These models offer valuable tools for data interpretation in clinical diagnostics and decision-making processes. Consequently, researchers emphasize the utility of both machine learning and deep learning methods for disease screening. This study aims to leverage both machine learning and deep learning techniques to classify ASD cases using a dataset sourced from the UCI repository. The dataset encompasses pediatric cases. The classification task employed k-nearest neighbors’ algorithm (k-NN), support vector machine (SVM), and convolutional neural network (CNN). Among these, CNN outperformed SVM and k-NN, achieving a remarkable accuracy of 99.71%.

articleTitle: Automated Table Detection Using R-CNN: A Cloud-Based Approach
abstract: In today's data-driven world, there is an ever-increasing requirement for effective data processing from document images that contain tables. These documents contain a wide variety of complexity, such as different layouts and visual distortions. This paper presents solution for table detection from document images by proposing deep learning models such as RCNN and MobileNetV2. The deep learning models were enhanced by intensive hyper-parameter tuning to optimize model parameters. In this research work experimentation is done on the Table bank dataset to demonstrate model performance. In addition to this, the paper emphasizes on practical deployment through Microsoft Azure. The work presented here represents a substantial improvement in the process of automating the detection of tables inside document pictures.

articleTitle: Smart Wearable for the Visually Impaired
abstract: The visually impaired always have a problem maneuvering through places without colliding with obstacles. They have to memorize the neighborhood and then walk around on assumption. According to the National Library of Medicine, India has the highest number of visually impaired people in the world, with an estimated 4.95 million blind persons and 70 million visually impaired. The leading causes of blindness in India are cataract, refractive errors, and glaucoma. As we are constantly surrounded by billboards, posters and direction sign boards, it's easy for a fully abled person to move around but visually impaired people do not have braille for their assistance at all times. Our research introduces an advanced device harnessing the power of Deep Learning models. The Real Time Audio descriptions, powered by OCR and Image Captioning, enhance users' awareness, while Video Call Assistance provides instant communication guidance. The objective of our project is to bridge the accessibility gap and enable a normal life for people with visual impairment by providing an all inclusive, user friendly device. The proposed device is equipped with a microprocessor unit, camera module and capacitive touch sensors, which convert the captured image to audio output, thus enhancing accessibility for individuals with visual impairments.

articleTitle: Secure File Transfer on Cloud Using Blockchain and Encryption
abstract: Cloud computing has become a potent and adaptable tool for distant data access and storage in recent years. However, security worries have also grown as cloud services are used more often. For enterprises and individuals, safe information sharing and storage in the cloud have become a key concern. This research article suggests a unique method for improving cloud file transfer security by combining blockchain technology's advantages with encryption. We outline a theoretical framework and discuss how combining blockchain technology with encryption methods might improve data security, reliability, and accessibility in the cloud.

articleTitle: Characterizing Neural Network Weights for Class Imbalanced Learning
abstract: Exploring the weight space of the neural network can lead to insights about how the network makes decisions. However, interpreting information within the weight space poses significant challenges, representing an active and complex area of ongoing research. This study is driven by the motivation to explore the hidden patterns in the weight space. The motivation of the study is to understand the weight space by characterizing the pattern space of the original and augmented samples, utilized for oversampling the underrepresented class in imbalanced learning. The major contribution of this paper is to address the fundamental task of highlighting the metrics that effectively characterize the pattern space. This characterization is the interim approach toward the motivation of our study regarding understanding the weight space of a neural network. Moreover, this research provides a comprehensive exploration of the potential pitfalls associated with each metric, along with detailed experiments and results.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Robotics: A Scalable and Versatile Mobile Robotic Arm for Modrn Applications
abstract: In response to the growing demand, warehouse sizes are increasing, posing challenges for manual and semi-automatic storage and retrieval systems. While static programmable robotic arms have been used extensively, they have limitations in the work envelope, reliance on wired accessories, and difficulty in relocation. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a 3D-printed, wirelessly operated 5-DOF mobile robotic arm with AI capabilities. The arm, featuring 5 revolute joints and 6 servo motors, is lightweight yet structurally robust, printed with ABS filament using the Fused Deposition Method for its high tensile and compressive strength. Mounted on a mobile platform, the arm facilitates pick-and-place tasks across the facility. The mobile platform, equipped with sensors, ensures situational awareness and can operate in surveillance mode, utilizing deep learning for facility supervision, and monitoring temperature, humidity, and harmful gas levels. The entire system can be wirelessly accessed, controlled, and automated via a webpage over the internet or a local network. Overcoming challenges faced by static robotic arms, this versatile prototype finds applications in handling hazardous objects, navigating treacherous environments, as well as surveillance and monitoring.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Prediction Using Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: This research aims to predict energy consumed per person by applying various Machine Learning Algorithms. Many vital factors like Energy intensity, access to electricity, GDP growth, renewable energy, etc. are taken into account that contribute in determining global energy consumption patterns and can help in tracking the progress of various countries towards sustainable development. The dataset taken is a highly comprehensive account of all the countries and showcases various indicators for sustainability spanning multiple years, from 2000 to 2020. To help in the prediction of energy consumed per person, various machine algorithms like Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Decision Tree Regressor, Random Forest, Gradient Booster and XG Booster have been used. Apart from the commonly used error rate, the model best suited for the dataset is decided on the basis of bias-variance tradeoff. Feature Engineering is also applied and its effect on the error rate and bias-variance is observed. The results obtained from this research can be used to forecast future energy needs, help in the formulation of energy policies, and in efficient resource allocation.

articleTitle: OMS - CRM Application for B2B FMCG Business
abstract: In today's highly competitive business environment, B2B FMCG businesses face significant challenges in managing their operations and maintaining strong customer relationships. To address these challenges, many businesses are turning to OMS-CRM applications. These applications combine order management systems with customer relationship management tools to provide a comprehensive platform for managing orders, inventory, and customer interactions. This research paper investigates the impact of OMS-CRM applications on B2B FMCG businesses. The study examines the benefits of implementing an OMS-CRM application, including improved order accuracy, increased efficiency, and enhanced communication with customers. The research also explores the challenges associated with implementing OMS-CRM applications and provides recommendations for successful implementation. The findings of this study suggest that implementing an OMSCRM application can lead to significant improvements in sales revenue and customer satisfaction in the B2B FMCG industry. By streamlining operations, automating processes, and enhancing communication with customers, businesses can increase efficiency and reduce errors, ultimately leading to increased revenue and improved customer loyalty. This research paper provides valuable insights into the benefits and challenges of implementing OMS-CRM applications in the B2B FMCG industry and offers practical recommendations for successful implementation.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of UV Spectroscopy for Measurement of Bone Mineral Density
abstract: The quantitative assessment of the mineral makeup and density of bone tissue is known as bone density measurement. It is a diagnostic technique for evaluating the strength and stability of bones, particularly for conditions like osteoporosis. Osteoporosis is a state where the human bone has a lower than necessary bone density which usually occurs in elder humans. A condition where the bone is so brittle that a normal strike on the bone can cause fractures and ruptures and the bone density usually degrades with age people in society above the age of 50 are commonly affected with osteoporosis as from what is seen. This study looks into the viability and precision of measuring bone absorbance using UV light as an alternative technique. The goal is to determine whether using UV light instead of more traditional methods, including dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and quantitative ultrasound (QUS), could have advantages in determining bone density. As older people seem to be affected by X-ray-based scans due to various old age sensitivity reasons as the treatment and diagnosis on an orthopedic platform is very much carried out for such people, a less harmful UV light sensing technique can be much better in terms of radiography effects. DXA scans involve the use of X-rays, which expose patients to ionizing radiation. UV light-based densitometers provide a radiation-free alternative, making repeated measurements safer and reducing potential long-term radiation risks due to less scan time. The investigation involves passing UV light through a sample of bone material. The UV light passes through the bone minerals and is absorbed by them. The higher the bone density, the higher the absorption detected, and the output side is measured with a lower light intensity. Over a range of wavelengths, an analysis employing a UV-visible spectrophotometer, bone powder, and human bone absorbtivity is assessed. As a result, we are creating testing equipment to assess UV light absorption as it passes through a bone sample using UV sensors.

articleTitle: Forecasting of financial time series data possessing stable distributions by employing Stochastic Differential Equations: A review
abstract: The paper acknowledges the complex behaviour of time series data, renowned for its inherent chaotic nature and inclination towards sudden, significant high jumps. To address such intricate data, the incorporation of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with noise can be done to accurately represent the data and its inherent traits. To better comprehend the distribution sustained by the data, the paper explores the realms of stable distribution, particularly relevant for data exhibiting heavier tails. Therefore, this review highlights the utility of modelling white noise within the frame work of a non-Gaussian distribution governed by Lévy motion. In this context, it proposes using alpha stable Lévy motion due to its remarkable ability to closely mirror the data's characteristics. Thus harmonizing the noise modelling process with the data's intricate dynamics. It aims at the techniques proposed in various research papers and discerning the most effective approach for analyzing financial time series data. Additionally, it also outlines the major improvements and future implementations in this domain.

articleTitle: Harnessing Machine Learning for Predictive Analysis of Air Quality in Pune City: A Comparative Study
abstract: With urbanization and industrialization propelling at an unprecedented rate, monitoring and predicting air quality has become an imperative task for ensuring public health and environmental safety. While traditional methods for air quality prediction often rely on deterministic models and historical patterns, the emergence of machine learning (ML) offers a promising avenue for enhancing prediction accuracy. In this study, we harness the power of multiple ML techniques, ranging from classical regression models to sophisticated deep learning architectures, to predict the Air-Quality-Index (AQI). By utilizing comprehensive datasets sourced from renowned environmental agencies, we aim to provide a comparative analysis of the performance and efficiency of each model. For this endeavor, our primary focus was on the Pune region, with datasets specifically obtained from stations located at Karve Road, Nal Stop, Swargate, Bhosari, and Pimpri. Preliminary findings suggest that certain ML techniques exhibit heightened predictive capabilities, outperforming conventional methods. This paper provides insights into the potential of ML in environmental forecasting, laying the groundwork for future research in the domain.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Citrus Greening Disease Recognition in Oranges using CNN and Random Forest
abstract: To identify the citrus greening disease in oranges, this study provides a combined strategy using Convolutional Neural Networks (also known as CNNs) and Random Forests. Images of citrus leaves can be extracted with the help of the CNN architecture, which uses three layers of convolution and maximum pooling layers. The classification accuracy of the CNN is improved by a random forest, a collaborative learning method. Extensive tests on a dataset of disease-free and infected citrus fruit leaves show how effective the suggested method is in detecting illness with high accuracy. To recognize the citrus greening disease early and reliably, CNN and Random Forest integration provide a nondestructive and effective method. This helps to manage citrus farms sustainably. The findings of this study hold significant implications for the citrus industry, offering a non-destructive, rapid, and cost-effective solution for disease detection. The combination of advanced machine learning techniques, including CNNs and Random Forest, presents a promising avenue for future research in agricultural disease recognition and management.
